is_anopheles.evidence: The study exclusively investigates Aedes aegypti ('Evolution of kdr haplotypes in worldwide populations of Aedes aegypti: Independent origins of the F1534C kdr mutation', page 1).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The study genotypes Aedes aegypti voltage-gated sodium channel mutations (P989S, I1011M, V1016I/G, T1520I, F1534C) rather than the required Anopheles target resistance markers.

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: No genotype or allele counts are reported for target Anopheles resistance markers.

african_field_population.evidence: Although African populations of Aedes aegypti were sampled, no Anopheles mosquitoes were included.

is_primary_study.evidence: It is a primary empirical study sequencing NaV amplicons in mosquito populations.

sub_country_location.evidence: Specific sampling localities are named, such as Sedhiou in Senegal and Nairobi in Kenya (page 6).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Collection years are specified for population samples (e.g. 2001-2015 for Brazilian samples, page 8).

duplicate_risk.evidence: DNA samples were derived from existing lab collections from earlier genetic studies, but are analysed here via amplicon sequencing of NaV.

supplement.evidence: Supplementary tables contain Aedes aegypti data and are not required since the study species is out of scope.

assessment.summary: This study evaluates the origin and evolutionary dispersal of kdr haplotypes in worldwide populations of the arbovirus vector Aedes aegypti using next-generation amplicon sequencing. Because it focuses entirely on Ae. aegypti and does not test any Anopheles species or target Anopheles resistance markers, it is not eligible.
exclusion_reasons: The study investigates Aedes aegypti and does not evaluate any Anopheles mosquitoes.
The study does not report any of the required Anopheles insecticide resistance target markers.
